themes_detail.label: Street sweeping collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK, up 860% from a 0.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.72), suggesting a sudden breakdown in sanitation service delivery across Bushwick.
evidence: 6 street sweeping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (860% spike, z-score 7.72)
Coincides with repeated CB budget request for 'Other capital budget request for DSNY,' suggesting chronic understaffing
This is the most recent spike in the dataset, emerging within the current reporting week
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to determine if there was a service interruption, staffing shortage, or equipment failure this week
Walk affected blocks to document street conditions; interview residents about trash accumulation
Cross-reference with Heat/Hot Water complaints (1968 total) to see if DSNY crews are being redirected to emergency services

themes_detail.label: Park noise surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints in parks jumped to 5 THIS WEEK, up 700% from a 0.6 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 6.29), indicating a sharp increase in disruptive activity at Bushwick's public spaces.
evidence: 5 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score 6.29)
Aligns with CB's repeated requests for 'new or expanded park or amenity' — suggests existing parks may be under-maintained or under-supervised
Bushwick Inlet Park development is ongoing (Hell Gate, 2026-04-02), potentially creating tension over limited green space
reporting_angles: Visit parks cited in complaints to observe noise sources and time of day; interview park-goers and nearby residents
Examine Parks Dept. staffing levels and enforcement presence in Bushwick parks this week
Investigate if noise complaints cluster around specific parks (e.g., Bushwick Inlet Park construction zones) or times (evenings/weekends)

themes_detail.label: Water system crisis emerging
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints spiked to 110 TWO WEEKS AGO, up 547% from a 17.0 weekly average (z-score: 11.51), marking the highest-severity statistical anomaly in the dataset and suggesting potential citywide or neighborhood-specific water infrastructure failure.
evidence: 110 water system complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 17.0 weekly baseline (547% spike, z-score 11.51 — highest severity in dataset)
Heat/Hot Water remains top complaint category with 1968 complaints over 90 days, suggesting water issues persist
Plumbing complaints (379 total) rank #10, likely cascading from underlying water system failures
reporting_angles: Request DEP data on water main breaks, pressure loss events, or boil water advisories in CD 304 from 2 weeks ago to present
Interview affected residents about water outages, discoloration, or pressure loss; document impacts on buildings dependent on hot water systems
Determine if water spike correlates with Heat/Hot Water complaints (1968 total) — investigate whether landlords failing to maintain boilers due to water issues
Check if spike has subsided or if 110-complaint level represents new baseline

themes_detail.label: Illegal dumping surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints surged to 39 TWO WEEKS AGO, up 322% from a 9.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.25), revealing a sharp rise in environmental violations that aligns with Bushwick's repeated CB requests for green infrastructure and sanitation improvements.
evidence: 39 illegal dumping complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 9.2 weekly baseline (322% spike, z-score 6.25)
CB repeatedly requests green infrastructure and stormwater management evaluation, suggesting environmental degradation is chronic priority
Unsanitary Condition (497 total complaints) ranks #7 in 90-day volume, indicating systemic cleanliness issues
reporting_angles: Map the 39 dumping complaints from 2 weeks ago to identify hotspot locations; document what materials are being dumped
Investigate DSNY enforcement response rate and penalties issued for illegal dumping in Bushwick during that period
Interview residents near dump sites about public health impacts and whether city clean-up has occurred since complaints were filed

themes_detail.label: Graffiti escalation
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 23 TWO WEEKS AGO, up 261% from a 6.4 weekly average (z-score: 6.94), signaling a potential outbreak of vandalism or decline in enforcement across Bushwick neighborhoods.
evidence: 23 graffiti complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 6.4 weekly baseline (261% spike, z-score 6.94)
Illegal dumping and graffiti spikes within same 2-week window suggest broader environmental management breakdown
Street sweeping emergency this week may indicate city is only now responding to cascading environmental complaints
reporting_angles: Document current graffiti conditions on streets and buildings cited in complaints 2 weeks ago; assess whether it remains or has been addressed
Interview NYPD and Sanitation about enforcement activities and gang/crew involvement in tagging patterns
Investigate whether specific neighborhoods (Williamsburg vs. central Bushwick) are more affected
